q.t: What is an open chord?
o: A chord that uses some open strings
A chord with no fingers at all
q.e: Open chords sit in the first frets and let some strings ring open.

q.t: Em in TAB (low E → high e) is…
q.e: Fingers on the A and D strings at fret 2.

q.t: E major in TAB (low E → high e) is…
q.e: Like Em plus finger 1 on G string fret 1.

q.t: From which string do you strum the D chord?
q.e: D's root is the open D string — strum the top four strings.

q.t: From which string do you strum the C chord?
q.e: C's root is at fret 3 of the A string.

q.t: Which chord is played x 0 2 2 1 0?
q.e: A open, D 2, G 2, B 1, high e open = A C E = A minor.

q.t: Which chord is played x 0 2 2 2 0?
q.e: Three fingers at fret 2 on D, G and B = A major.

q.t: Which chord is played 3 2 0 0 0 3?
q.e: Low E fret 3 = G, A fret 2 = B, high e fret 3 = G → G major.

q.t: How many strings do you strum for E, Em and G?
q.e: Their roots are on the low E string, so all six ring.

q.t: Which pair differ by only one finger moving one fret?
q.e: Em → E: just add finger 1 on the G string, fret 1.

q.t: Which chord is played x x 0 2 3 2?
q.e: D, A, D, F♯ = D major.

q.t: Which chord is played x x 0 2 3 1?
q.e: D, A, D, F = D minor.

q.t: Which chord is played x 3 2 0 1 0?
q.e: C, E, G, C, E = C major.

q.t: A and Am differ on which string?
q.e: B string fret 2 = C♯ (A major); fret 1 = C (A minor).

q.t: D and Dm differ on which string?
q.e: High e fret 2 = F♯ (D major); fret 1 = F (D minor).

q.t: In every major/minor pair (E/Em, A/Am, D/Dm), the note that changes is the…
q.e: Major 3rd ↔ minor 3rd. Everything else stays.

q.t: Changing C ↔ Am, which fingers can stay down?
q.e: Finger 1 (B fret 1) and finger 2 (D fret 2) are in both. Only finger 3 moves.

q.t: Why should the low E string be left out of the D chord?
o: It would put a non-root note at the bottom
It is out of tune in D
q.e: A chord sounds steadiest with its root as the lowest note. D's root is the D string.

q.t: Why look for fingers that can stay down when changing chords?
q.e: Each finger that stays is one less thing to place in time.

q.t: Am and E use the same finger shape. How?
o: E is the Am shape moved one string over
E is Am played one fret higher
E is Am with an extra finger
q.e: Move the whole Am shape one string toward the thick strings and you have E.

q.t: What notes are in the open G chord (3 2 0 0 0 3)?
q.e: G, B, D, G, B, G — only three note names.

q.t: What notes are in the open C chord (x 3 2 0 1 0)?
q.e: C, E, G, C, E.

q.t: What note does the A string play in the G chord (fret 2)?
q.e: A → A♯ (1) → B (2). B is the 3rd of G.

q.t: What note does the B string play in the C chord (fret 1)?
q.e: B → C at fret 1 — the root again.

q.t: What note does the D string play in the C chord (fret 2)?
q.e: D → D♯ → E. E is the 3rd of C.

q.t: What is the lowest note of the C chord?
q.e: The low E is not played, so the lowest note is C on the A string.

q.t: In the A chord, the high e string is open. Which chord note is it?
q.e: A major = A C♯ E. E is the 5th.

q.t: In the D chord, which string plays the 5th (A)?
q.e: G → G♯ → A at fret 2.

q.t: Why is the 'x' over the low E in Am?
o: E is not the root — A should be lowest
E is not in the Am chord
The low E is too loud
q.e: E is in Am (A C E), but as the lowest note it makes the chord unsteady. Starting on the A root sounds solid.

q.t: Your C chord has a dead high e string. What is the most likely cause?
o: The high e is out of tune
You strummed from the A string
The amp gain is too low
q.e: Finger 1 on the B string often touches the high e. Arch it so it lands on its tip.

q.t: Which open chord has its root on the D string?
q.e: The open D string is the root of D and Dm.

q.t: Which open chord has its root on the A string at fret 3?
q.e: A string fret 3 = C.

q.t: Which of these chords contains the note G♯?
q.e: E major = E G♯ B.

q.t: Which of these chords contains the note F♯?
q.e: D major = D F♯ A.

q.t: Which of these chords contains the note B?
q.e: G = G B D. (C = C E G, Dm = D F A, A = A C♯ E — no B.)

q.t: G (G B D) and Em (E G B) share which notes?
q.e: Two notes in common — that's why G and Em sound close and swap well.

q.t: C (C E G) and Am (A C E) share which notes?
q.e: Two shared notes — and the fingers for them (1 and 2) stay down when you change.

q.t: You play D but it sounds muddy with a low E in it. What happened?
o: The high e is out of tune
D doesn't use the B string
q.e: The open low E isn't the root of D. Start the strum on the D string or mute the low E with your thumb.

q.t: Which chord change needs only one finger to move?
q.e: C ↔ Am: fingers 1 and 2 stay; only finger 3 moves.

q.t: Why does A minor sound sadder than A major, though they look almost the same?
o: Its 3rd is a half step lower (C instead of C♯)
It is played on lower frets
q.e: A minor 3rd (3 half steps) instead of a major 3rd (4) — the whole difference in mood.
